body:
Stacked on #5809, which derives the lexer position lazily for seekable input. Only the top commit belongs to this PR. ## What Pretty-printed JSON indents every line with a run of spaces, and `skip_whitespace()` read them one character at a time. For contiguous input (`bulk_scan`: pointers, `std::string`, `std::vector` and similar), the lexer now skips the spaces after a newline in 8-byte steps, directly in the input buffer. `lexer::skip_indentation()` loads 8 bytes, XORs them with `0x2020…20` and skips whole words of spaces. On the first word that is not all spaces, it also skips that word's leading spaces using a count of trailing zeros. Tabs, `\r`, the last 7 bytes of the input and anything that is not a space go through the existing byte loop. The skip bypasses `get()`. That is safe because `bulk_scan` implies `lazy_position` from #5809: the position comes from the adapter, so nothing has to be counted per character. Streams, files, wide strings and user-defined adapters are unchanged. The idea comes from Glaze's `skip_matching_ws`, which compares against the previous line's indentation. Comparing against spaces is simpler (no state) and handles any indent width. Changes: - `detail/input/lexer.hpp`: adds `skip_indentation()`, called after `'\n'` in `skip_whitespace()`. - `detail/bit_ops.hpp`: adds `count_trailing_zeros()`, using `__builtin_ctzll` or a portable fallback (the fallback was checked against the builtin for 640k values). - `docs/home/architecture.md`: one sentence about the bulk-scan interface. ## Performance Medians of 60 runs, in µs. "Lazy" is #5809 and "this" is this PR. The x86 machine is a VPS with some background load, so differences under about 4% are noise there. | file | | GCC 13 x86-64
lazy → this | clang 18 x86-64
lazy → this | Apple clang 21 arm64
lazy → this | |---|---|---|---|---| | twitter, indent 2 | parse | 5151 → 5032 (−2%) | 5150 → 5145 (0%) | 1863 → 1758 (−6%) | | | accept | 1334 → 1261 (−5%) | 1253 → 1253 (0%) | 661 → 580 (−12%) | | twitter, indent 4 | parse | 5270 → 5001 (−5%) | 5455 → 4930 (−10%) | 1915 → 1790 (−7%) | | | accept | 1567 → 1297 (−17%) | 1486 → 1201 (−19%) | 770 → 602 (−22%) | | citm_catalog, indent 2 | parse | 7795 → 7585 (−3%) | 7900 → 7240 (−8%) | 3157 → 3008 (−5%) | | | accept | 2438 → 2126 (−13%) | 2185 → 1928 (−12%) | 1189 → 993 (−16%) | | citm_catalog, indent 4 | parse | 8360 → 7726 (−8%) | 8234 → 7159 (−13%) | 3470 → 3068 (−12%) | | | accept | 3106 → 2164 (−30%) | 2533 → 1985 (−22%) | 1424 → 1041 (−27%) | | twitter, minified | parse | 4767 → 4851 | 4786 → 4702 | 1726 → 1719 | | | accept | 1160 → 1123 | 1041 → 1130 | 564 → 563 | | citm_catalog, minified | parse | 7226 → 7101 | 6763 → 6734 | 2860 → 2943 | | | accept | 1835 → 1699 | 1554 → 1533 | 915 → 903 | Minified input never reaches the new code and is unchanged within noise. On x86, the minified accept cells varied by 4–8% between sweeps. I also measured a version that skips only whole 8-byte words. It was 5–12% slower on `accept` and gave nothing on 2-space indentation, where runs are often shorter than a word. That is why the partial word is finished with the trailing-zero count. ## Tests - New test case in `unit-deserialization.cpp`. For indentation runs of 0 to 33 spaces, it checks that contiguous and stream input give the same result, byte offset and message in seven layouts: a value after the indent, an error after it, the run ending at the end of the input, tab/CR mixed in, a comment after the indent, and an unexpected second value. Two cases also have fixed expected messages. Mutants that skip one byte too many or start one byte late fail this test. - `count_trailing_zeros()` gets checks next to the existing `count_leading_zeros()` test in `unit-class_lexer.cpp`. - Differential check against #5809, run locally and not committed. It covered 89k inputs and found byte-identical results, error messages, SAX events and positions, and diagnostic positions: - 742 corpus files, also re-indented with 1, 2, 4, 8, 9 and 16 spaces and with tabs - truncations and byte mutations of those files, half of them inside indentation - 42k generated edge cases - each input parsed as pointer range, `std::string`, `std::string_view`, vector and stream, with comments off and on, and with `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS` off and on - also run under ASan/UBSan, with no findings ## Breaking changes None. This only changes how fast whitespace in contiguous input is skipped. Results, error messages and positions are identical. `count_trailing_zeros()` is a new `detail` helper. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Skip the indentation after a newline 8 bytes at a time
